strengths: The six CRITICAL issues from the pessimistic review are each resolved with a principled mechanism rather than a workaround: CRITICAL-1 resolves host-visibility by mandating the TRANSFER_WRITE->HOST_READ barrier path-identically on both coherent and non-coherent paths and both queue modes, plus an unconditional NonCoherent host-side invalidate after the fence wait; neither relies on the fence-signal host-domain guarantee as a substitute. This is the correct and conservative reading of Vulkan spec §7.5 and §11.2.4 combined. Reference: https://registry.khronos.org/vulkan/specs/latest/html/vkspec.html#memory-device-hostaccess

CRITICAL-2 (ownership-transfer barrier range mismatch — the canonical NVIDIA-passes/AMD-corrupts class) is eliminated by the design itself, not patched: device-local buffers are created VK_SHARING_MODE_CONCURRENT over {compute_family, transfer_family} in DedicatedTransfer mode, so there are zero queue-family ownership-transfer barriers anywhere. This is structurally sound per Vulkan spec §12.7.4 (CONCURRENT sharing mode). The only cost is a potential minor driver-compression penalty on the device-local buffer — a correct trade-off for a first dedicated-queue implementation. Reference: https://registry.khronos.org/vulkan/specs/latest/html/vkspec.html#resources-sharing

CRITICAL-3 + CRITICAL-4 (semaphore lifecycle and partial-submit error recovery) are resolved together by (a) making timeline semaphore the primary path with a monotonically increasing AtomicU64 counter that makes reuse-hazard structurally impossible, and (b) a fully specified error-recovery matrix (technical_spec §4.C) covering all three mid-chain failure cases with device_wait_idle + CB-per-pool cleanup + binary semaphore recreation. The matrix covers: upload-fail, upload-ok/compute-fail, upload-ok/compute-ok/readback-fail, and fence-timeout. No CB leak, no hang-on-never-submitted-fence. This matches the pattern used by wgpu-hal's queue submission error recovery.

CRITICAL-5 (cross-queue deadlock) is resolved by atomic-group submit serialization: the context-level queue_submit_lock is held across all THREE submits of one dispatch as a single atomic group, released before any host fence wait. The formal deadlock-freedom proof in technical_spec §4.D is correct: because the three submits of a dispatch are issued under one lock, the GPU enqueue order on T and C cannot interleave two dispatches' chains, making the wait-for graph over {T,C} acyclic. This is a well-known pattern — CONCURRENT sharing eliminates the release/acquire hazard, and atomic-group serialization eliminates the cross-queue head-of-line block. Reference: Vulkan synchronization spec §7.4 and the Khronos synchronization examples repo.

CRITICAL-6 (unsafe impl Sync unsoundness) is corrected: PersistentMapping is now Send-only (never Sync), with a PRIVATE *mut u8 and no public host_ptr. All host access goes exclusively through copy_in/copy_out called under the per-handle buffers Mutex. The SAFETY argument in technical_spec §1.C correctly observes that Mutex<Vec<BufferSlot>>: Sync requires Vec<BufferSlot>: Send, which is satisfied by PersistentMapping: Send — and no Sync is required or claimed. This matches the established Rust pattern for 'pointer moves with its owner, derefed only under a Mutex'. Reference: Rustonomicon unsafe send/sync section.

The acceptance-honesty gap (pessimistic VIOLATION-1/2) is addressed with the four-force-option AT-1418 oracle: running the same kernel through single-queue-coherent / dedicated-queue / forced-non-coherent / forced-binary-semaphore and asserting byte-identical output turns forced-non-coherent from security-theater into a real regression detector on coherent hardware. The fault-injection variant in AT-1409 (dropped flush causes divergence) proves the non-coherent code path is load-bearing. The bounded, acknowledged gap (TRUE non-coherent requires EB.1 AMD/Intel CI) is explicitly documented in design_md_additions — this is the correct honest posture for M3.0.

All WARNING fixes are confirmed in revision_changelog: WARNING-1 (non_coherent_atom_size plumbed from props.limits, never hardcoded), WARNING-2 (.min(alloc) clamp bug removed; correct rule is WHOLE_SIZE when align_up>=alloc), WARNING-3 (one-shot dispatch double-unmap impossible via consuming unmap), WARNING-4 (Vulkan12Features struct is named local binding, no dangling p_next), WARNING-5 (command_pool_lock for both shared compute and transfer pools), WARNING-6 (flush loop covers every uploaded slot, not just slot 0).

AT-1410 now explicitly includes atom_size in {1,64,128,256,1024,65536} and asserts (size%atom==0 OR offset+size==alloc), closing the pessimistic reviewer's test-adequacy gap on the WHOLE_SIZE boundary and the WARNING-2 clamp bug. AT-1412 now includes a watchdog timer explicitly guarding against the CRITICAL-5 hang scenario. AT-1419 covers partial-submit error recovery structurally. AT-1420 adds the 50 GB memory-cap assertion that was missing.

Public API preservation is unchanged from the r0 review: all existing public symbols (VulkanContext::new/new_with_options/physical_device_name/max_compute_work_group_count/prepare_kernel/dispatch_handle/dispatch, DispatchRequest, KernelHandle::{spirv_word_count,cache_key,buffer_sizes}) retain their exact signatures, confirmed against context.rs and kernel_handle.rs in the current codebase.

SPIR-V codegen remains untouched: spirv_capabilities_required and spirv_extensions_required are both empty; all new Vulkan features (timeline semaphore, HOST_CACHED memory, dedicated transfer queue) are runtime host-side decisions. spirv-val must remain clean and AT-1417 asserts it.
concerns: Observation (not a blocker): the instance API version bump to min(reported, 1.2) is correct for reaching VK_KHR_timeline_semaphore / Vulkan 1.2 timelineSemaphore. Lavapipe (Mesa >= 23) reports 1.3, so the timeline path gets single-queue CI coverage on Lavapipe. However, the timeline semaphore's upload_done / compute_done handoff is only USED on the dedicated-queue path; on single-queue Lavapipe, HandoffSemaphores will be Some(Timeline) but the three-CB split is not taken. This means AT-1412 (multi-handle concurrent, dedicated path with watchdog) and AT-1413 (dedicated vs single byte-equal) can only run on hardware with a dedicated transfer family. The CI coverage gap is documented and acknowledged — this is the bounded EB.1 gap explicitly stated in the design. No action required for M3.0.

Observation (not a blocker): the binary-semaphore error-recovery (recreate two binary semaphores on U-ok/C-fail) requires destroy+create inside the recovery path, under device_wait_idle. This is correct and matches the stated CRITICAL-3/4 resolution. The Coder must ensure this recreation happens only in the Binary SyncMode branch and is guarded by the per-handle buffers Mutex (which it is, since recovery is inside record_and_submit_dispatch under the mutex). This should be easy to implement correctly given the explicit coder_handoff_notes guidance but is a subtlety worth the Coder noting.

Observation (not a blocker): the open_question about CONCURRENT vs EXCLUSIVE perf on the RTX PRO 6000 is correctly left open. If the 1 ms / 2 ms saxpy_1m / q4km_512 gates are missed specifically because CONCURRENT disabled a driver compression pass, the design already documents M3.1 as the right place to revisit EXCLUSIVE+ownership-transfer with real AMD/Intel CI. Reviewers agree CONCURRENT is the right first-implementation default.
validation_against_existing: CONCURRENT sharing mode decision confirmed against Vulkan spec §12.7.4: 'Resources created with VK_SHARING_MODE_CONCURRENT must only be accessed by queues from the queue families that are specified.' No ownership-transfer barriers are needed; only execution+memory dependencies via semaphores. Reference: https://registry.khronos.org/vulkan/specs/latest/html/vkspec.html#resources-sharing

Persistent-map-once pattern confirmed in VulkanMemoryAllocator documentation: VMA_ALLOCATION_CREATE_MAPPED_BIT keeps the mapping alive for the buffer lifetime and is the recommended approach for staging buffers accessed from the host. Reference: https://gpuopen-librariesandsdks.github.io/VulkanMemoryAllocator/html/group__group__alloc.html#gga4fceecc301f4064dc808a43c4905f2aca9166e73a6e51d43e9f89ea7b36e671d5

HOST_CACHED + flush/invalidate pattern confirmed in Vulkan spec §11.2.4: 'If the host cache is not coherent, the application must call vkFlushMappedMemoryRanges after writing to mapped memory before submission, and vkInvalidateMappedMemoryRanges after the device has written to the mapped memory before reading.' Flush-before-submit and invalidate-after-fence is exactly the placement specified. Reference: https://registry.khronos.org/vulkan/specs/latest/html/vkspec.html#memory-device-hostaccess

Timeline semaphore with monotonic AtomicU64 counter confirmed in VK_KHR_timeline_semaphore spec: 'Timeline semaphore signal and wait operations take a 64-bit integer value ... Signal operations must provide monotonically increasing payload values.' The reserve_timeline_block() atomic-advance-by-2 pattern means no two dispatches can use the same values even on error paths. Reference: https://github.com/KhronosGroup/Vulkan-Docs/blob/main/proposals/VK_KHR_timeline_semaphore.adoc

The atomic-group-submit deadlock-freedom proof in technical_spec §4.D matches the standard analysis for ordered submission on shared FIFO queues: if two dispatch chains cannot interleave at the enqueue level, no cross-dispatch cyclic wait edge can form. This is consistent with the synchronization guidance in 'Vulkan Synchronization Explained' by Maister (Hans-Kristian Arntzen). Reference: https://themaister.net/blog/2019/08/14/yet-another-blog-explaining-vulkan-synchronization/

The Send-only unsafe impl pattern for a struct holding a raw pointer, where the pointer is only dereferenced under a Mutex, is the standard Rust approach validated in the Rustonomicon §Send and Sync section. Mutex<Vec<BufferSlot>>: Sync requires Vec<BufferSlot>: Send but NOT Sync, so PersistentMapping: Send is sufficient and correct. Reference: https://doc.rust-lang.org/nomicon/send-and-sync.html

Current codebase confirmed: context.rs line 192 uses VK_API_VERSION_1_1 (will be bumped to min(reported,1.2)); buffers.rs allocate_staging_buffer (lines 295-362) uses HOST_VISIBLE|HOST_COHERENT (will be superseded by allocate_staging_buffer_cached); kernel_handle.rs Drop (lines 162-174) does NOT call vkUnmapMemory before destroy_buffer (coder_handoff_note DROP ORDERING covers this gap); DispatchQueueCtx (context.rs line 531-534) currently holds only command_pool and queue (will gain transfer, queue_mode, atom_size, three locks per the spec). All deltas are real new requirements, not redundant spec.

summary: All four prior optimistic gaps are confirmed closed in the r1 revision: queue_submit_lock is explicitly listed in context.rs additions, force_noncoherent_staging is in VulkanContextOptions with env read, the drop-ordering coder handoff note is precise and structurally enforced by consuming unmap, and VK_EXT_host_memory_alloc_placement + BDA are explicitly documented as deferred in both the spec and design_md_additions. The r1 revision also resolves all six pessimistic CRITICAL issues without introducing feasibility regressions: CONCURRENT sharing eliminates the ownership-transfer barrier class entirely, timeline-primary monotonic semaphores eliminate reuse hazards, atomic-group submit serialization with a formal deadlock-freedom proof eliminates cross-queue head-of-line blocking, the full error-recovery matrix covers every mid-chain failure, and Send-only guarded PersistentMapping is correct Rust. The four-force-option AT-1418 byte-exact oracle converts the acceptance-honesty gap from a risk into a documented, bounded gap with a clear EB.1 AMD/Intel follow-up. The 21 acceptance tests (AT-1400 through AT-1420) are measurable by existing bench IDs, the public API is preserved byte-for-byte, and codegen/SPIR-V are untouched. The design is APPROVED for implementation.
